answer: Retrospective Value-Compatibility Clustering. Each identity’s transaction history is embedded as a vector of counterparties, assets, and contract calls; clusters whose internal similarity is high but whose external linkage is near zero are flagged as likely sock-puppet timber. Enforcement is post hoc: flagged clusters lose accumulated reputation and payouts. To survive, an attacker must diversify each identity’s economic island with genuinely distinct counterparties and behaviors, and maintain that divergence over a grove of accounts—raising per-identity operating cost sharply.
